For a first-order reaction: rate = k₁[A]
For a second-order reaction: rate = k₂[A]²
For a zero-order reaction: rate = k₀

When we have parallel reactions (competing reactions from the same reactant), the ratio of products depends on the ratio of reaction rates.

If we have a first-order reaction competing with a second-order reaction:
- At high concentrations of [A], the second-order term [A]² will be much larger than the first-order term [A], so the second-order reaction will be favored.
- At low concentrations of [A], the first-order term will be relatively larger than the second-order term, so the first-order reaction will be favored.

In general, at high reactant concentrations, reactions with higher order are favored, while at low reactant concentrations, reactions with lower order are favored.
